open-question.question: Does the task-list tool require the fixed first-line heading of each task file it writes to (# TASKS TODO or # TASKS DONE), refusing with one Error: line a file whose first line is anything else, or does it treat whatever stands before the first ## section as opaque content that it carries through unchanged and never checks?
open-question.recommendation: The whole-file render decision already parses a task file into its heading line and its sections and re-emits the heading region in canonical layout, which closes Opaque Preamble's byte-for-byte carry-through and settles the rewrite-or-splice condition this option's drawback hung on, so writing the fixed heading on every render is the one rule that needs no preamble slot in the model, no repair rule, and no refusal path that could stop a headless completion over a cosmetic first line, matching how the tool already heals a missing separator and blank-line drift silently; its one cost, dropping text a person put above the first section, concerns a case no task file in the repository shows, and since every writer commits its own write the drop is recorded in that commit's diff and recoverable by revert.
open-question.alternative: The tool never refuses over the preamble and never checks it. On every write to a task file it discards whatever stands before the first ## section and writes the fixed heading for that file plus one blank line in its place, so every file the tool has touched starts with the canonical preamble. Initialize does the same for TASKS_TODO.md as part of its whole-file replacement. The files heal themselves: a damaged, missing, or altered heading is corrected on the next write and never blocks a run, and the task files converge on the shape define_milestone.py creates without anyone having to repair them by hand. Any text a person put above the first section is silently dropped on the next completion or submission, with nothing printed, and only the commit diff shows it, which is the silent loss the tool's contract otherwise avoids. Whether rewriting bytes outside the section being written fits depends on the whole-file-rewrite-or-splice axis owned by a sibling question.

Before any insert, append, or move, the tool checks that the first line of each task file it is about to write is exactly its fixed heading (# TASKS TODO for TASKS_TODO.md, # TASKS DONE for TASKS_DONE.md). Any other first line, an empty file included, is refused with one Error: line naming the file, and both files stay byte-for-byte unchanged. Anything else standing between that heading and the first ## section is carried through unchanged and never checked. Initialize keeps its recorded behaviour of replacing TASKS_TODO.md whole, writing the heading itself, so it does not check the old first line. It catches a file that is not a task file at all, such as a truncated, overwritten, or hand-mangled one, before the tool splices sections into it. It costs nothing today, since all 92 task files in the repository's 46 milestone directories start with exactly the heading define_milestone.py writes, and it still leaves any note a person adds under the heading alone. The tool picks both paths itself from MILESTONE_DIR, so a swapped or wrong file can only come from a hand edit, and the check mostly guards a case that never occurs. It also makes a cosmetic edit to the heading line, like a changed case or a trailing word, a hard stop for every completion, submission, and append until someone repairs the line by hand. It adds one more refusal path that needs its own tests.

The tool checks the whole preamble, not just its first line, before any insert, append, or move. Everything before the first ## section must be exactly the fixed heading for that file followed by nothing but blank lines. A different first line, an empty file, or any other text in the preamble is refused with one Error: line and both files left byte-for-byte unchanged. Initialize keeps replacing TASKS_TODO.md whole and checks nothing. The files keep exactly the shape define_milestone.py creates and the task format describes, so no text outside a ## section can slip in unnoticed. The tool's own parser never has to decide what non-section text before the first heading means. A note a person adds under the heading, which is harmless to every reader of the files, blocks every write to that file until it is removed by hand. That makes it the strictest option and the one most likely to stop a headless completion chain over a cosmetic detail. The preamble is also checked by a rule that nothing else in the workflow states or needs.

The tool never checks the heading. Whatever stands before the first ## section in a task file, whether the fixed heading, other text, or nothing at all, is treated as opaque content and carried through byte-for-byte on every insert, append, and move. Initialize keeps its recorded behaviour of replacing TASKS_TODO.md whole with the fixed heading followed by the list. It adds no refusal path and no rule beyond the ## and --- sections the tool actually works on. A hand edit above the first section never blocks a completion or a submission, and the tool's job stays limited to the sections it moves and inserts, which is all the decisions recorded so far define. A task file whose top has been damaged or replaced is written into without complaint, so the corruption carries forward silently until a person or a reading skill notices it. The fixed heading becomes a convention that only define_milestone.py and initialize enforce, and the first-line contract nothing else checks drifts with every hand edit.

The tool never refuses over the preamble. On every write to a task file it makes sure the first line is the fixed heading for that file. If the first line is a single-# heading with different text, the tool replaces it with the fixed heading. If the file starts with anything else, such as a ## section, plain text, or nothing, the tool inserts the fixed heading and a blank line above it. Any other preamble text is carried through unchanged. A missing or altered heading is repaired without ever blocking a run, and unlike rewriting the whole preamble it keeps any note a person added under the heading. It needs a repair rule (replace or insert) that is more complex than either checking the heading or ignoring it, and that rule has to be tested. It still rewrites a line outside the section being written without saying so, which depends on the whole-file-rewrite-or-splice axis owned by a sibling question. A file that is not a task file at all gets a heading added on top of it instead of being refused.

open-question.question: When a later write re-parses a task file whole, how does the tool treat a body line that an earlier insert wrote verbatim and that reads as a `---` separator or a `## ` heading: as structure, so the section ends or splits there, or as part of its section, and by what parsing rule?
open-question.recommendation: One bounded lookahead and no parser state removes the only failure the tool's own verbatim output could inflict on later writes, a body `---` line that under the plain rules strands text and leaves every later initialize, insert, and move refusing until a hand edit the sole-writer contract forbids, while a body `## ` line opens a section under every unfenced rule alike and cannot be told from a heading without contradicting the decision that an unterminated section ends at the next heading; the fence exemptions buy fence state, an unclosed-fence hazard, and a second test surface under both interpreters for a construct no task file in the repository holds, and the reading of "its `---` line" as the one standing directly before the next heading or the end of the file is pinned in the tests and CLAUDE.md.
open-question.alternative: A `---` line is a separator only when the next non-blank line is a column-0 `## ` heading or the end of the file; any other `---` line is body text of its section. Every column-0 `## ` line is a heading, with no code-fence exemption, so a section without a qualifying `---` ends at the next heading as the section-boundary decision states. Each section holds at most one qualifying `---`, nothing is ever stranded between sections, and no write refuses for this reason. The rule covers bodies and `**Verified:**` bars alike. Fully resolves body `---` lines with one bounded lookahead and no new state: a verbatim body `---` stays inside its section through every later re-parse and canonical render, so no write ever refuses or misplaces text because of one, and the recorded boundary rule keeps its meaning for real separators. A body `## ` line still opens a new section on the next re-parse, silently turning part of a brief into a phantom task in `TASKS_TODO.md`; the rule also reads "its `---` line" in the boundary decision as the last `---` before the next heading, a reading tests and `CLAUDE.md` must then pin.

Every line that reads exactly `---` (trailing whitespace ignored) is a separator and every column-0 line starting `## ` is a heading, wherever it stands, with no code-fence exemption. The rule applies alike to an inserted body, a body carried through by a move, and a `**Verified:**` bar piped verbatim. A body `## ` line therefore opens a new section on re-parse, and a body `---` line ends its section there. Non-blank text left between such an early `---` and the next heading belongs to no section, so any later write that parses the file refuses with one `Error:` line naming the section, with the file unchanged. Insert's "never treated as structure" holds only for the insert call itself. It is the simplest parser and the most literal reading of the recorded section-boundary decision: one line test per line, no lookahead and no fence state, and it gives the same verdict a reader skimming the raw Markdown would. The tool's own verbatim output can break the file for later writes: a body `## ` line silently becomes a phantom task in `TASKS_TODO.md` that `complete-all-tasks` would pick up and the uniqueness check would count, and a body `---` makes every later initialize, insert, or move refuse until someone edits the file by hand, which undercuts the tool being the sole writer.

Same line tests as the plain rule (an exact `---` line is a separator, a column-0 `## ` line is a heading, stranded text after an early `---` makes later writes refuse with one `Error:` line), except that lines inside a fenced code block are always body: a column-0 line opening with three or more backticks or tildes starts a fence that the next matching fence line closes, and a fence still open at the next real heading or at end of file closes there. The rule covers bodies and `**Verified:**` bars alike. Keeps the plain rule's literal reading for ordinary prose while protecting the one place structural-looking lines legitimately appear in a brief or an acceptance bar, quoted examples such as a YAML front-matter block or a sample task section inside a fence. Adds fence state to the parser and its tests, yet still splits on or refuses for a bare `## ` or `---` line outside a fence, so the phantom-task and stuck-file failures remain for unfenced bodies, and an unclosed fence opened in one body changes how the following lines parse.

A `---` line is a separator only when the next non-blank line is a column-0 `## ` heading or the end of the file, every other `---` line being body, and a column-0 `## ` line is a heading unless it stands inside a fenced code block (a column-0 line of three or more backticks or tildes opening a fence that the next matching fence line closes, an unclosed fence ending at the next real heading or end of file). Lines inside a fence are never structure, and a section without a qualifying `---` ends at the next real heading. Nothing is stranded and no write refuses for this reason; the rule covers bodies and `**Verified:**` bars alike. Gives the widest protection any rule compatible with the recorded decisions allows: body `---` lines are always safe, and `## ` lines are safe wherever an author has quoted them in a fence, so the insert-time promise that body lines are never structure survives later writes in every case except a bare `## ` line in prose. The most parser state and test surface of the set (lookahead plus fence tracking, both pinned under two interpreters), and a bare unfenced `## ` line in a body still splits the section into a phantom task, since a heading cannot be told from body text without contradicting the decision that an unterminated section ends at the next heading.
